title: Strict chain-level Roos comparison for an exact product-preserving functor
statement: Let C,D be small sites with commutative sheaves of rings R,S and module categories A,B, with exact countable products. Let F:A\to B be exact and additive with invertible canonical countable-product comparisons. Fix functors HA from complexes of strict A-towers to complexes of A and HB similarly for B. Assume their objects are Cone(1-s)[-1], with exactly the signed coordinates H(X)^(p+1)=P_X^(p+1)\oplus P_X^p specified by the shift/cone isomorphisms followed by (id,-id), and assume their maps are the diagonal product maps in those coordinates. Then there are isomorphisms psi_X:F(P_X)\cong P_FX and kappa_X:F(HA(X))\cong HB(FX). The projections of psi_X are F(pr_n). Each of the two signed-coordinate projections of kappa_X, followed by pr_n, is F of the corresponding projection of HA(X). For every strict tower chain map f:X\to Y, F(HA(f)) kappa_Y=kappa_X HB(F(f)). Notions: [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-inverse-system], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

proof.text: Take the canonical product comparison degreewise. Its projection identities imply that it commutes with differentials and with the tower shift, hence with 1-s. The cone comparison for an additive functor, followed by this commuting square, and the shift comparison give kappa. Transport by the two object equalities. In the signed coordinates its two components are the product comparison, which proves the displayed equations. Apply product projections to the two components for a strict tower map to obtain naturality. The inverse uses the inverse product comparison on both coordinates, so kappa is an isomorphism.

        biprod.map
          ((Limits.Pi.map (fun n : ℕ ↦ (HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map
            f).app (op n))).f (p + 1))
          ((Limits.Pi.map (fun n : ℕ ↦ (HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map
            f).app (op n))).f p))) :
